name: Adobe Firefly
tagline: Generative images, video, vectors, and effects integrated with Adobe apps

pricing.notes: Working normalization from the official public pricing structure. Recheck the source page immediately before publication.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: Free daily image/video/audio generations; Adobe does not publish a numeric daily generation count

tiers.name: Firefly Standard
tiers.limits: 2,000 credits/month; up to 20 five-second videos, 6 minutes of translation, or 200 sound-effect generations
tiers.notes: Individual plan is sold monthly; no individual annual option is shown.

tiers.name: Firefly Pro
tiers.limits: 4,000 credits/month; up to 40 five-second videos, 13 minutes of translation, or 400 sound effects

tiers.name: Firefly Pro Plus
tiers.limits: 10,000 credits/month; up to 100 five-second videos, 33 minutes of translation, or 1,000 sound effects
tiers.notes: Current first-year promotional price is $34.97/month through 2026-08-26; it then renews at the regular $49.99/month unless canceled.

tiers.name: Firefly Premium
tiers.limits: 50,000 credits/month; unlimited Firefly Video Model generations, 166 translation minutes, or 5,000 sound effects
tiers.notes: Current first-year promotional price is $139.91/month through 2026-08-26; it then renews at the regular $199.99/month unless canceled.

tiers.name: Firefly Pro for teams
tiers.limits: 4,000 credits/month per license with team administration

tiers.name: Firefly Pro Plus for teams
tiers.limits: 10,000 credits/month per license with team administration

tiers.name: Firefly Premium for teams
tiers.limits: 50,000 credits/month per license with team administration

pricing.freeTierCaps: Free plan: daily refreshed image/video/audio generations, but Adobe does not publish the numeric daily cap.
pricing.billingTerms: individual plans monthly only; team plans use an annual commitment billed monthly
pricing.hiddenCosts: Monthly generative credits do not roll over. Add-on credit plans start at 2,000 credits. Promotional Pro Plus/Premium prices rise to the regular monthly price after the first year; third-party partner models can consume credits at different rates.

verdictSummary: Do not mistake the interface for the product. Adobe Firefly's durable value is proprietary model, inference, which a solo one-shot build cannot reproduce responsibly. The prompt therefore builds only the closest honest personal consolation tool.
coreLoopDIY: Build the closest honest personal generative creative tools console around a locally available image model, with prompt history and file export.
diyTimeEstimate: not a true replacement; consolation build in one to two days
replacementScope: consolation build only; the paid product's moat remains
requirements: GPU-capable machine or user-provided inference API
model weights obtained under their own licence
Explicit README warning that this is a consolation build, not a production replacement
whatYouLose: high-fidelity color, format, and export handling
licensed training data and style tuning
whyPeopleStillPay: Adobe Firefly: The interface is replaceable. The subscription buys the model, aesthetic tuning, inference fleet, safety work, and rapid improvement.
ongoingBurden: Own model downloads, GPU compatibility, queueing, safety choices, storage, and changing model licences.

notes: Credibility row: Adobe Firefly survives for a structural reason, not because its interface is difficult to copy.
prompt:
Build the closest honest consolation tool inspired by Adobe Firefly; do not claim to replace its structural moat.
Use exactly this stack: Python 3.12 + FastAPI + ComfyUI API + React.
Primary job: Build the closest honest personal generative creative tools console around a locally available image model, with prompt history and file export.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: high-fidelity color, format, and export handling; the vendor's proprietary model quality; licensed training data and style tuning.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
